bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Delays in MMR land acquisition; regulatory approvals for Nagpur Mall; execution risk in residential handovers; LTCG tax impact (12.5% without indexation) on asset sales; reliance on single strategic pivot for future growth
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Despite high occupancy, retail revenue growth is primarily from leasing, not sales; the company is effectively transitioning from a mall operator to a real estate development fund using asset sales as a capital recycling engine
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Strategic sale of 100% shares in the operational mall assets (Ch Sambhaji Nagar & Coimbatore) at a valuation of INR 1,242.5 Cr gross consideration, described as unlocked "at highly attractive exit yield".
- Stated target utilisation of the proceeds is to "Acquire project in Premium MMR market" and to "invest in High Value High growth projects in MMR".
- Deck flags the proceeds as net of leverage and tax: "Significant cash generation (post-debt and LTCG adjustments)" — it does not quantify the net figure.
- Deck notes the Finance Act, 2024 revised the LTCG tax rate to 12.5% without indexation benefit on transfer of a long-term capital asset, and the Group remeasured its deferred taxes with the impact taken to the P&L in the quarter and year ending Mar25.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- cost position: land bought early and held without debt, keeping the cost base fixed for everything built on it — evidence: land bank of 11.89 million square feet, all fully paid up, with no acquisition liability suits against any of it
- customer lock-in: proven ability to keep destinations full for a decade after opening — evidence: Prozone Mall Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar and Prozone Mall Coimbatore reached 94% and 96% occupancy respectively in Q4 FY2026
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Input cost inflation absorbed rather than passed on — WPI inflation reached 9.68% in May 2026 (basic metals inflating 12%) against retail inflation of only 3.93%, so cost increases have been largely absorbed rather than passed on, and construction margins carry that gap.
- Occupancy already near peak at both malls — Occupancy at Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar and Coimbatore stood at 94% and 96% respectively, so further growth must come from rental escalation and tenant mix rather than from filling vacant space.
- Loss-making Outright Sales segment retained after the profitable Leasing segment is sold — The Outright Sales segment recorded a loss in FY2026, and the Company retains that segment while divesting the profitable Leasing (mall) segment.
- Weak urban consumer sentiment — The RBI's Consumer Confidence Survey shows the urban Current Situation Index in pessimistic territory, and mall footfall and tenant sales depend on discretionary spending.
- Policy and regulatory sensitivity — The real estate sector is inherently sensitive to policy changes on interest rates, tax regimes, subsidies and housing schemes, which can directly influence borrowing costs, consumer sentiment and profitability.
- Brand reputation risk — As a developer of retail and residential destinations, Prozone's brand reputation is central to its success; negative publicity, adverse events or heightened competition could impact trust and positioning.
- Execution risk on the pending mall disinvestment — As at the date of the most recent disclosure, completion of the proposed disinvestment had not occurred, and FY2027 outcomes depend on completing it and applying the proceeds to debt reduction and Mumbai acquisitions.
- External macro risk from prolonged West Asia conflict and monsoon — ICRA identifies prolonged conflict in West Asia as the principal downside risk to residential demand estimates, and the RBI identifies a deficient south-west monsoon as a risk to rural demand and water availability.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Deck frames a "Strategic Pivot to MMR": focus toward Grade A Office and Retail platforms in prime Mumbai CBD locations, on the view that "Mumbai has had Infra boom expected to improve realty potential".
- Operating portfolio is two regional malls — Prozone Mall, Ch Sambhaji Nagar and Prozone Mall Coimbatore — which the deck says are "monetized at Peak Performance" and "BOTH PROPERTIES ARE OPERATING AT PEAK OCCUPANCY."
- Development portfolio spans Coimbatore residential, Nagpur residential (with retail), and Indore plotted residential township, i.e. a build-and-sell arm alongside the lease-rental arm.
- Nagpur asset is pitched on catchment: "4.5m catchment population"; Indore is described as a "Prominent business and industrial centre in Madhya Pradesh" with "1.9m city population".

- [Community/footfall driver] Both malls run a heavy events calendar as footfall drivers — SVEEP voting awareness, Republic Day, Fit India Carnival (SAI), Gudi Padwa and the Ajanta-Ellora International Film Festival at Ch Sambhaji Nagar; Pongal, Women's Day laser & butterfly show, Vookie Eco Fest and a startup gathering at Coimbatore.

outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body: Coimbatore Residential: 402/540 units sold (Rs 2,167 mn); Nagpur Residential: 254/336 units sold (Rs 1,780 mn); Indore Phase 1B: 54/75 plots under EOI
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Nagpur Mall (0.5m sqft retail + 0.39m sqft development potential); Indore township (43.5 acres, Phase 2+); MMR CBD land acquisition using Rs 1,242.5 Cr disinvestment proceeds
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Redirect capital from the two mature, disinvested malls toward acquisitions in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, favouring Grade A office and retail platforms.
- Prefer redevelopment/acquisition structures over greenfield land acquisition in Mumbai, since entry price rather than land ownership determines returns in a supply-scarce market.
- Deploy capital in stages rather than as a single commitment, reporting on each stage as it happens.
- Retain and accelerate the residential and plotted developments at Coimbatore, Nagpur and Indore (more towers, faster phases) and monetise them at the earliest sensible point.
- Grow without carrying heavy leverage once the portfolio transition is complete; hold assets only when surplus cash flow makes holding a choice rather than a strain.
- Consolidated full ownership of the operating subsidiaries (ending the fifteen-year foreign joint-venture partnership) as a prerequisite for agile, decisive corporate decisions.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's expansion is now centred on the Mumbai Metropolitan Region: having consolidated full ownership of its operating subsidiaries and resolved to divest its two mature malls (Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar and Coimbatore), it intends to redeploy the proceeds into Grade A office and retail platform acquisitions in Mumbai, entering by acquisition/redevelopment rather than greenfield development, and deploying capital in stages. Separately, on the retained portfolio, at Coimbatore Phase 1 has two of seven towers built with the third under construction (approximately 1.9 million sq ft total residential development); at Nagpur a plotted development project of 0.14 million sq ft is under development with 2.69 million sq ft of additional balance development potential; and at Indore, development of Phase 1B of the plotted township is in progress.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Mumbai Metropolitan Region retail stock is supply-constrained (17.45 million sq ft stock against a pipeline of only about 4 million sq ft to 2031), which the company expects to support pricing power for owners of existing quality stock and to favour acquisition over greenfield development as the realistic route to scale.
- Institutional appetite for stabilised Grade A retail is estimated at USD 25-30 billion, supported by rising hybrid revenue-linked lease structures and longer lease tenures, which the company reads as improving the pool of buyers for quality income-yielding assets.
- Residential demand is trading up in value even as volumes stay flat, with the luxury segment's share of sales rising, which the company expects to support pricing on its retained residential portfolio at Coimbatore, Nagpur and Indore.
- Office demand from Global Capability Centres is expanding into Tier-2 markets including Coimbatore and Indore, cities where the company already holds land.
- Input cost inflation (WPI, basic metals) is flagged as the main near-term threat, squeezing construction margins since cost increases have been largely absorbed rather than passed on.
- Management expects the input cost pressure that squeezed FY2026 margins to ease during FY2027 if global oil and non-fuel commodity price projections hold.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Prozone Realty is strategically monetizing high-performing retail assets in Tier-II cities to redeploy capital into premium Grade-A residential and retail projects in Mumbai's CBD, leveraging peak occupancy and strong footfall to unlock value. The shift from asset-heavy operations to capital-efficient development positions it for margin expansion and higher ROCE in India's most resilient real estate market.

Once the current portfolio transition is complete, the Company intends to grow without carrying heavy leverage.

The Company intends to accelerate its retained residential developments at Coimbatore, Nagpur, Indore and Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar with more towers and faster phases, monetising these holdings at the earliest sensible point.

At Nagpur, a plotted development project of 0.14 million sq ft is under development, with a further 2.69 million sq ft of additional balance development potential.
At Indore, development of Phase 1B of the plotted township (43.5 acres total) is in progress.
The Company intends to use proceeds from the proposed mall disinvestment to acquire a project in the premium Mumbai Metropolitan Region market, with a focus on Grade A office and retail platforms.

Residential: Coimbatore (540 units, 87+ handed over), Nagpur (336 units, 209 handed over), Indore (Phase 1A: 74 plots completed, Phase 1B: 75 plots under sales)

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Retail:** Prozone Mall, Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar, Prozone Mall, Coimbatore
- **Residential:** Coimbatore residential development (Phase 1), Nagpur residential development, Indore township (plotted development)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Tier-2 Indian cities (Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar, Coimbatore, Nagpur, Indore)
- Mumbai Metropolitan Region

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Coimbatore Residential: 402/540 units sold (Rs 2,167 mn); Nagpur Residential: 254/336 units sold (Rs 1,780 mn); Indore Phase 1B: 54/75 plots under EOI

guidance.title: Guidance / outlook
guidance.body: Strategic pivot toward high-yield MMR developments using proceeds from strategic disinvestment of Ch Sambhaji Nagar and Coimbatore malls; targeting premium residential and retail projects in Mumbai CBD.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Nagpur Mall (0.5m sqft retail + 0.39m sqft development potential); Indore township (43.5 acres, Phase 2+); MMR CBD land acquisition using Rs 1,242.5 Cr disinvestment proceeds

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Mumbai Metropolitan Region retail stock is supply-constrained (17.45 million sq ft stock against a pipeline of only about 4 million sq ft to 2031), which the company expects to support pricing power for owners of existing quality stock and to favour acquisition over greenfield development as the realistic route to scale.
- Institutional appetite for stabilised Grade A retail is estimated at USD 25-30 billion, supported by rising hybrid revenue-linked lease structures and longer lease tenures, which the company reads as improving the pool of buyers for quality income-yielding assets.
- Residential demand is trading up in value even as volumes stay flat, with the luxury segment's share of sales rising, which the company expects to support pricing on its retained residential portfolio at Coimbatore, Nagpur and Indore.
- Office demand from Global Capability Centres is expanding into Tier-2 markets including Coimbatore and Indore, cities where the company already holds land.
- Input cost inflation (WPI, basic metals) is flagged as the main near-term threat, squeezing construction margins since cost increases have been largely absorbed rather than passed on.
- Management expects the input cost pressure that squeezed FY2026 margins to ease during FY2027 if global oil and non-fuel commodity price projections hold.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin: 48.1% (FY26), up from 32.2% (FY25); EBITDA excluding other income margin: 39.3% (FY26); cost control driven by high occupancy and rental stability; no material cost inflation cited

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: 100% of Rs 1,242.5 Cr from strategic sale of two malls to be redeployed into premium MMR residential/retail projects; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; debt reduction not prioritized over growth capex

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company's expansion is now centred on the Mumbai Metropolitan Region: having consolidated full ownership of its operating subsidiaries and resolved to divest its two mature malls (Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar and Coimbatore), it intends to redeploy the proceeds into Grade A office and retail platform acquisitions in Mumbai, entering by acquisition/redevelopment rather than greenfield development, and deploying capital in stages. Separately, on the retained portfolio, at Coimbatore Phase 1 has two of seven towers built with the third under construction (approximately 1.9 million sq ft total residential development); at Nagpur a plotted development project of 0.14 million sq ft is under development with 2.69 million sq ft of additional balance development potential; and at Indore, development of Phase 1B of the plotted township is in progress.

litigation.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)
litigation.body: {"material": false, "note": "The company states its land carries no acquisition liability suits against any of it (Corporate Overview / 'The Land').", "as_of": "2026-09-08"}

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- cost position: land bought early and held without debt, keeping the cost base fixed for everything built on it — evidence: land bank of 11.89 million square feet, all fully paid up, with no acquisition liability suits against any of it
- customer lock-in: proven ability to keep destinations full for a decade after opening — evidence: Prozone Mall Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar and Prozone Mall Coimbatore reached 94% and 96% occupancy respectively in Q4 FY2026

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Delays in MMR land acquisition; regulatory approvals for Nagpur Mall; execution risk in residential handovers; LTCG tax impact (12.5% without indexation) on asset sales; reliance on single strategic pivot for future growth

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Despite high occupancy, retail revenue growth is primarily from leasing, not sales; the company is effectively transitioning from a mall operator to a real estate development fund using asset sales as a capital recycling engine

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Redirect capital from the two mature, disinvested malls toward acquisitions in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, favouring Grade A office and retail platforms.
- Prefer redevelopment/acquisition structures over greenfield land acquisition in Mumbai, since entry price rather than land ownership determines returns in a supply-scarce market.
- Deploy capital in stages rather than as a single commitment, reporting on each stage as it happens.
- Retain and accelerate the residential and plotted developments at Coimbatore, Nagpur and Indore (more towers, faster phases) and monetise them at the earliest …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Shareholding] As of Mar 26 the pattern is Promoters 53.56%, FPI 3.05%, Others 43.39% (source: BSE), with named key investors ACACIA Group 3.01%, Radhakishan Damani & Family 0.90% and Sandeep Raheja Group 4.23%.
- [Community/footfall driver] Both malls run a heavy events calendar as footfall drivers — SVEEP voting awareness, Republic Day, Fit India Carnival (SAI), Gudi Padwa and the Ajanta-Ellora International Film Festival at Ch Sambhaji Nagar; Pongal, Women's Day laser & butterfly show, Vookie Eco Fest and a startup gathering at Coimbatore.

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.
